text:
Good afternoon, and happy Wednesday. First, the news from home.

Story one. According to MyJoyOnline and Graphic Online, the N P P has filed a suit at the Supreme Court seeking an interpretation of constitutional provisions governing presidential term limits. The party wants the court to clarify whether a presidential term limit means a maximum of two terms, whether consecutive or non-consecutive.

Story two. Graphic Online reports that the Minority in Parliament has called for the immediate resignation of Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa over alleged financial irregularities in the evacuation of one thousand nine hundred and sixty-four Ghanaians from South Africa. The Minority Ranking Member on Parliament's Committee on Foreign Affairs, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, also demanded an independent audit and threatened parliamentary proceedings for a vote of censure.

Story three. MyJoyOnline and Three News report that former President John Agyekum Kufuor has backed a proposal to extend the country's presidential term from four to five years. He argued that the additional year would give governments more time to implement their policies and development projects.

Now, around the world.

Story four. The Guardian and France Twenty-Four report that at least sixty-four people have been killed in central Spain after a high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped on the tracks. Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente gave details at a press conference following the disaster, which is the second major high-speed train accident in Spain this year.

Story five. The Guardian and Africanews report that Tanzania has announced its first natural gas discovery in a decade, with an estimated two hundred and twenty-three billion cubic feet found at the Kasa-one X S T two well in the Mnazi Bay area. The country's energy minister described the discovery as a major milestone for the East African nation.

You can open Dad News and ask for more about any story by its number.
